conversation.user: I just want to renovate one cold, damp bedroom, about 300 sq. ft. of wall area, to stop mold. Can I use this inside, and will it eat up my room space?
conversation.assistant:
Yes, you can absolutely use hempcrete as an interior thermal retrofit on your cold, damp bedroom wall to naturally regulate moisture and stop mold. It won't eat up much space either—for an interior insulation layer, we typically recommend a slim 2.5 to 3-inch thickness, which requires roughly 2.5 to 3 m³ of material installed between furring strips using hand-tamping. Best of all, hemp-lime is 100% legal, 0% THC, fire-resistant, and completely unrelated to recreational marijuana. Just keep in mind that these numbers are planning estimates, not stamped engineering or permit advice. 

What type of existing wall construction are you currently dealing with behind that cold surface?
